procedure: Reaction conditions as printed in Scheme 2 of the source: N-(2,6-Dimethylphenyl)chloroacetamide (0.1 mmol), diethylamine (1.5 equiv), KI (10 mol %), solvent (0.1 mL), 30 min, oil bath temperature. procedure: Two-step, one-pot procedure, conditions as printed in Scheme 3 of the source: (i) 2,6-dimethylaniline (5.0 mmol), chloroacetyl chloride (1.1 equiv), MeCN (10 mL), 40 C, 30 min; (ii) K2CO3 (2.2 equiv), room temperature, 30 min; (iii) diethylamine (1.1 equiv), KI (10 mol %), reflux, 1 h. As described in the text: chloroacetyl chloride (1.1 equiv) was first added dropwise to a solution of 2,6-dimethylaniline in acetonitrile and was heated for 30 min at 40 C to achieve full acylation of the aniline. Potassium carbonate (2.2 equiv) was added, and the solution was stirred for an additional 30 min at 40 C. Potassium iodide (10 mol %) and diethylamine (1.1 equiv) were subsequently added, and the reaction mixture was refluxed for 1 h and subjected to the same workup conditions as in procedure B. In this two-step, one-pot reaction (Procedure C, p S12), Lidocaine was obtained as a white solid in 85% yield. The temperature recorded here is the reflux point of acetonitrile, 82 C, which is the step the yield is reported for.

procedure: Method 1 (room temperature), quantities as printed in the source: suspend 0.05 g of theobromine in 1.5 mL of MeOH; dissolve it fully using 0.03 g of sodium methoxide in MeOH as the base; add 0.6 mL of CH3I with a 1 mL syringe, in a fume hood. The mixture is stirred at room temperature and followed by TLC at 30, 60 and 90 minutes, eluting with dichloromethane/methanol 95:5. On completion the solvent is evaporated, the residue is partitioned between CH2Cl2 and water, the organic layer is dried over sodium sulphate and the solvent evaporated, to give a silky white solid (0.048 g, 90%). The product is identified by comparing its melting point with that of an authentic caffeine standard, m.p. 234-236 C. Transcribed from the published quantities and steps; the article is open access at the DOI.
